content.title: "SkyKing": The stolen plane, a barrel roll and a shocking end over Puget Sound
content.text: PORTLAND, Ore. (KATU) — A man was seriously injured, and another man was charged with attempted murder after a street fight in North Portland.READ MORE | Detectives share new details in case of woman found dead in car with her unharmed babyAccording to court documents, Portland police responded to the Denny’s at 11950 N. Center Ave. on reports of a man who had been gashed in the throat.A witness told police he was outside the Denny’s when he heard yelling in the nearby street and saw one man stumble backward while the other fell as if he had been pushed.The witness said he helped the injured man into the restaurant after noticing a large slash in his throat.The suspect, later identified as Christopher James Parkins, 39, was described as living nearby under an underpass and as being 5 feet 10 inches tall, wearing a red or orange shirt and having tattoos.Police later found Parkins and took him into custody. They said he had a 3- to 4-inch fixed-blade knife in his hand, partially concealed by his sleeve.After being advised of his Miranda rights, Parkins allegedly told police he had been awake for several days and frequently smoked methamphetamine.According to court documents, he said he could not remember the attack. “Everything feels like it’s not even real.”He said all he could remember was hiding in a bush and hearing sirens. He also said he had whiskey the night before at a bar near the Denny’s but could not remember how long he was there.He told police he recently lived in Oak Grove but lost his housing and was living on the streets.According to police, the victim’s injuries were very severe, and the slash to his throat was so deep that his trachea was exposed.Parkins was arraigned Monday on charges of attempted murder, first-degree assault and unlawful use of a weapon. He remains held without bail and also faces a parole violation.According to court records, Parkins has prior convictions, including assaulting a public safety officer in 2025 and methamphetamine delivery in 2017.Comment with BubblesJOIN THE CONVERSATION (18)He is due back in court April 28, according to court records.
